title: Core Web Vitals & Performance
description: Master LCP, FID, CLS metrics and learn how Next.js automatically optimizes them.

slides.title: What Are Core Web Vitals? 📏
slides.content:
# Google's Performance Metrics

Google uses three main metrics to rank page experience:

* **LCP (Largest Contentful Paint)** – loading speed. Should be < 2.5s.
* **FID (First Input Delay)** – interactivity. Should be < 100ms.
* **CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift)** – visual stability. Should be < 0.1.

Good scores improve SEO and user satisfaction.

Next.js has built‑in features to optimize all three.

slides.title: LCP: Pre‑rendering & Image Optimisation ⚡
slides.content:
# How Next.js Helps LCP

* **SSG/ISR** – pages are pre‑built, so the HTML arrives instantly.
* **`next/image`** – lazy‑loads images, serves WebP/AVIF, sizes correctly, and uses `priority` for hero images.
* **`next/font`** – self‑hosts fonts, eliminating extra round trips.
* **CDN Caching** – static assets are served from edge locations.

All these reduce the time until the largest element (often a hero image or headline) appears.

quizData.question: What is the recommended maximum LCP time according to Google?
quizData.explanation: LCP should occur within 2.5 seconds from when the page first starts loading. Above 4 seconds is considered poor.

slides.title: FID: JavaScript & Hydration 🧠
slides.content:
# Making the Page Interactive Fast

* Next.js **code‑splits** by page – only the JS for the current page loads.
* **`next/dynamic`** – lazy‑load heavy components.
* **Server Components (App Router)** – zero client‑side JavaScript for static parts.
* **Hydration is optimised** – React 18's selective hydration.

FID is being replaced by **INP (Interaction to Next Paint)**, but the principle is the same: keep the main thread free.

slides.title: Dynamic Import with next/dynamic (components/HeavyChart.js)
slides.content: Defer loading a large chart library until it's needed.

quizData.question: What does `ssr: false` in `next/dynamic` do?

options.text: Disables the component on the server, loading it only on the client
Removes the component from the bundle

quizData.explanation: `ssr: false` tells Next.js to skip rendering this component on the server, useful for libraries that access browser APIs.

slides.title: CLS: Layout Stability 🏗️
slides.content:
# No More Janky Layouts

* **`next/image`** reserves space with `width`/`height` – no layout shift.
* **`next/font`** adjusts fallback font metrics to match the custom font.
* **Statically generated pages** have known dimensions.

CLS is often caused by dynamically injected ads or embeds. Reserve their space with aspect ratio boxes or `min‑height`.

slides.title: Measuring Performance 📊
slides.content: Use Lighthouse in Chrome DevTools, the Vercel Analytics dashboard, or the `web-vitals` library to track Core Web Vitals in production. Next.js provides a built‑in `next/analytics` on Vercel.
